deterministic.name: check-verifier-contract.py
deterministic.evidence: Manual source plus hash-verified existing controls: bash -n succeeds; tests/test.sh:60-61 writes initial zero/traps cleanup, probes before suites and exports APP_RESTART_HELPER at 193. However lines 152-178 can report restart readiness without terminating the old process or proving the new process owns the listener. Indexed original-term_ignored/app-restart.log:5,21 records EADDRINUSE followed by ready=1; raw results retain PID 34 and volatile-marker while helper exits 0. The extracted helper source matches the unchanged test.sh hash bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa. Cleanup lines 36-39 has an unbounded wait, confirmed by its 10-second killed control. Lines 224-225 also retain a gate-only graded=1/no_op=0 record after synthetic scored timeout/error. These are existing controlled harness observations, not a new security probe or configured app-judge run.
deterministic.method: manual documented behavior with cited parser/raw observations; private checker not executed
deterministic.counterexample: A non-durable server that ignores SIGTERM keeps its in-memory records in the old PID while the helper falsely announces a completed restart; the browser can consequently credit restart durability without a restart. A SIGTERM-ignoring child also stalls cleanup, and an evaluator scored-suite timeout is represented as graded application zero.
deterministic.suggested_fix: Escalate the shared harness defect for an approved common-baseline repair: bound cleanup, verify old-process termination and new-listener ownership, and distinguish suite failure from a completed grade; preserve canonical task files until that shared repair is authorized.
deterministic.run_verdict: CONFIRMED by unchanged-source synthetic helper/cleanup/suite controls; normal current golden restart also succeeds and does not refute the counterexample
